policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders the verb as an event happening to the silver cord itself -- 'before the silver cord is loosed' -- a breaking/snapping of the cord, which is the qere ירתק (rtq, of chains and cords); the ketiv ירחק (rhq) would mean the cord is removed or made distant, which the ASV wording does not express. The margin 'Or, snapped asunder' is classed alternative_rendering and is not relied on to decide, but it is consistent with the same lemma.
